hints: A positive cycle reachable from city 1 and able to reach city n can increase the score without bound.
Negate the score on each flight so maximizing becomes shortest-path minimization.
Run Bellman-Ford, then check whether a still-relaxable edge can lead to n.
analogy: A profitable loop matters only if you can reach it and still travel onward to the destination.
example: A positive-score loop at an isolated city cannot affect the best 1-to-n route.
correctness: Bellman-Ford detects reachable negative cycles after n-1 edge passes; reachability propagation filters cycles that cannot influence the destination.
algorithm: Compute which vertices can reach n by a reverse-graph search. Run Bellman-Ford from 1 for n-1 rounds on negated scores. If an edge can still relax from a reachable vertex into a vertex that can reach n, print -1; otherwise print the negated shortest distance to n.
